title: The Will of Little Hawley
premise: Estate lawyer Casper Coldharbour, who has quietly solved three deaths the police ruled accidental, is summoned to read the will of Edith Hawley—a will that shouldn't exist, since Edith died eleven years ago. When a drowned man washes up at Little Hawley dressed in clothes stolen from Casper's own closet, she realizes someone knows exactly who she is and wants her to stop investigating. To survive, Casper must reopen the one case everyone swore was closed: Edith's own drowning, which the tide is finally ready to give back. In the end, Casper exposes the surviving conspirator—Edith's son, who faked his mother's death to escape her fortune's terms—and chooses love over the duty that has kept her invisible.
about_author: R. M. Dravenmoor spent a decade as a probate clerk in coastal England before turning to fiction, and their mysteries are known for wills that lie and tides that remember. They live above a shuttered solicitor's office with a deaf terrier named Verdict.

chapters.title: The Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Casper Coldharbour's POV. She arrives at rain-soaked Little Hawley to read the will of Edith Hawley, dead eleven years by official record. The document is authentic; the signature matches. Emotional beat: professional unease curdling into dread as Casper realizes the paper in her hands is impossible.

chapters.title: Eleven Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: Casper's POV, flashback-tinged. She reviews how she solved three 'accidental' deaths without ever taking credit, staying deliberately invisible. Emotional beat: loneliness framed as discipline—the cost of being no one.

chapters.title: The House Remembers Her
chapters.summary: Casper explores Hawley House under the wary eye of housekeeper Mrs. Tarnow. Edith's room is preserved exactly as if she left yesterday, down to a half-finished letter. Emotional beat: intimacy with a dead woman who seems to have expected something.

chapters.title: The Beneficiaries
chapters.summary: Casper interviews the heirs: Edith's son Alistair, now a magistrate; niece Vera; and groundskeeper Pell. Each claims Edith drowned in 1979. None can explain the will dated 1984. Emotional beat: everyone performing grief they don't feel.

chapters.title: A Body Wearing My Clothes
chapters.summary: A man washes up on the shingle wearing Casper's stolen coat and scarf, a note in his pocket bearing her name. Police call it misadventure. Emotional beat: terror—invisibility has failed; someone is dressing a corpse as her.

chapters.title: Inspector Brightwater
chapters.summary: Local inspector Brightwater, who closed all three of Casper's past cases as accidents, suspects her connection to the body. Their sparring crackles with mutual recognition. Emotional beat: attraction sharpened by suspicion—two people who notice everything.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: Casper walks the tideline where the body was found and finds a woman's shoe, salt-eaten but old—Edith's size, Edith's year. Emotional beat: the sea beginning, at last, to give up what it took.

chapters.title: The Closed Case
chapters.summary: Casper pulls the 1979 file: Edith Hawley, drowned, case closed in four days. The coroner was Alistair's oldest friend. Emotional beat: cold anger at how easily a town agreed not to look.

chapters.title: Vera's Version
chapters.summary: Niece Vera, drink-loosened, recalls seeing Edith alive after the funeral date—but swears she saw a ghost and said nothing for decades. Emotional beat: guilt as inheritance; fear passed down like china.

chapters.title: Pell Knows the Grounds
chapters.summary: Groundskeeper Pell shows Casper an old boathouse with fresh padlocks and a floor scrubbed too clean. He warns her off in words that sound rehearsed. Emotional beat: menace beneath courtesy—the town closing ranks.

chapters.title: The Half-Finished Letter
chapters.summary: Casper deciphers Edith's unfinished letter: 'If you are reading this, I am already dead twice.' It names no one but promises proof hidden 'where the water cannot reach.' Emotional beat: Edith becomes a voice, urgent and afraid.

chapters.title: Someone Follows Me Home
chapters.summary: Casper notices a car tailing her from the archive office to her lodgings. She doubles back and finds the driver gone, engine warm. Emotional beat: hunted—the investigator realizes she is evidence now.

chapters.title: Brightwater's Doubt
chapters.summary: Brightwater privately admits the 1979 closure troubled him for years; he was young and told to sign. He offers Casper an uneasy alliance. Emotional beat: trust offered carefully, like a hand across a gap.

chapters.title: The Second Will
chapters.summary: In the firm's records Casper finds a codicil Edith signed in 1983, disinheriting Alistair unless he confessed to something unspecified. The codicil vanished from the file. Emotional beat: motive crystallizing—Alistair had everything to lose.

chapters.title: Dinner with the Magistrate
chapters.summary: Casper accepts Alistair's dinner invitation, trading courtesies laced with threats. He mentions her three solved cases by name. Emotional beat: the mask slips—he knows precisely who she is and what she does.

chapters.title: Ghost Light
chapters.summary: At night, a lamp burns in Edith's sealed bedroom. Casper and Brightwater find the window forced and the letter's page turned. Someone is reading over their shoulders. Emotional beat: violation—the dead woman's sanctuary breached.

chapters.title: Where Water Cannot Reach
chapters.summary: Following Edith's clue, Casper searches the dry-stone ice house above the flood line and finds a tin box: photographs, a train ticket dated after the death, and Edith's diary's final pages. Emotional beat: triumph cut short—the box is missing its most important item.

chapters.title: The Photographs
chapters.summary: The photos show Edith alive in 1984 at a seaside boarding house, and show Alistair visiting her there. The ticket confirms she fled her own funeral. Emotional beat: the case flips—Edith wasn't murdered then; she escaped.

chapters.title: Then Who Is in the Grave?
chapters.summary: Casper confronts the terrible question: whose body was buried as Edith Hawley? Records point to an unnamed woman washed ashore that same week. Emotional beat: horror reframed—an anonymous victim erased twice.

chapters.title: Mrs. Tarnow Breaks
chapters.summary: Housekeeper Tarnow confesses she helped Edith stage the drowning, believing it the only way to escape Alistair's control, and has guarded the secret out of love. Emotional beat: loyalty and betrayal braided together; grief finally given permission.

chapters.title: The Missing Page
chapters.summary: Tarnow reveals Edith returned secretly in 1990 to retrieve the rest of her diary—and never left. Alistair found her. Emotional beat: hope collapsing into certainty that Edith died here, in the house that remembers her.

chapters.title: Search of the Cellars
chapters.summary: Casper and Brightwater search Hawley House's cellars and find a bricked alcove behind the wine racks, recently mortared. Emotional beat: dread climbing with every step down.

chapters.title: Edith
chapters.summary: Behind the brick: remains, and with them the missing diary pages naming Alistair. Eleven years he kept her in the house. Emotional beat: sorrow and fury fused—the case everyone swore was closed opens like a wound.

chapters.title: Arrest and Reversal
chapters.summary: Brightwater moves to arrest Alistair, but the coroner's friend blocks the warrant; Alistair produces an alibi and counter-accusations against Casper, citing the drowned man in her clothes. Emotional beat: the trap snapping shut around her instead.

chapters.title: Framed
chapters.summary: Casper is suspended from her firm and named a person of interest. Her flat is searched; more of her belongings surface in the dead man's room. Emotional beat: isolation total—the invisible woman made visible as a suspect.

chapters.title: The Dead Man's Name
chapters.summary: Working alone, Casper identifies the drowned man: a retired archivist hired years ago by Edith to authenticate her will. He'd been asking questions in town for a week. Emotional beat: the pattern completing—everyone who touched the truth drowns.

chapters.title: Vera Runs
chapters.summary: Vera flees town after leaving Casper a note: 'He knows I talked.' Casper finds her at the rail station and convinces her to testify rather than run. Emotional beat: courage borrowed and returned—survival redefined as standing still.

chapters.title: Pell's Choice
chapters.summary: Pell admits Alistair paid him to lock the boathouse and burn a boat used in 1979, but he kept the boat's nameplate as insurance. He gives it to Casper. Emotional beat: a small man choosing, at last, a large thing.

chapters.title: The Nameplate
chapters.summary: The boat's name links to a 1979 ferryman who reported picking up a living woman matching Edith's description—and who died in a boating accident months later. Emotional beat: the third accidental death falling into place; Casper's old pattern confirming itself.

chapters.title: Brightwater Risks Everything
chapters.summary: Brightwater burns his career reopening the 1979 file officially, forcing exhumation of the grave marked Edith Hawley. Emotional beat: love declared through action, not words—duty and desire finally pointing the same direction.

chapters.title: The Wrong Woman
chapters.summary: Exhumation confirms the buried woman was not Edith: younger, unidentified. Casper traces her to a missing boarding-house maid, last seen with Alistair. Emotional beat: grief for the truly forgotten—justice owed to a nameless girl.

chapters.title: Alistair's Counterstroke
chapters.summary: Alistair has Tarnow's cottage set afire; Tarnow survives but recants in hospital, terrified. The town turns on Casper openly. Emotional beat: despair's floor—the price of survival made visible in other people's scars.

chapters.title: The Confession Tape
chapters.summary: Casper realizes Edith's tin box had a second compartment; returning to the ice house, she finds a wax-cylinder recording Edith made in 1984, naming Alistair's coercion and her plan. Emotional beat: the dead speaking at last—Edith engineered her own posthumous trial.

chapters.title: Reading the Will Aloud
chapters.summary: Casper formally reads the true will before witnesses: it conditions Alistair's inheritance on confession, and leaves the estate to whoever proves the truth. Emotional beat: ceremony as weapon—the law she serves becoming her sword.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Boathouse
chapters.summary: Alistair comes for the recording himself; Casper anticipated him. In the rising tide, he confesses while Brightwater records from hiding—then turns violent. Emotional beat: terror and resolve locked together as the water climbs.

chapters.title: The Tide Gives Up What It Took
chapters.summary: Struggle in the flooding boathouse; Brightwater saves Casper, and Alistair, fleeing, is caught by the same tide he used twice before. Emotional beat: climax—nature settling accounts no court could.

chapters.title: After the Water
chapters.summary: Alistair survives, broken and charged with two murders and the archivist's. The coroner's friend resigns. Casper's name is cleared publicly. Emotional beat: exhaustion after adrenaline; justice arriving unglamorous and real.

chapters.title: Two Funerals
chapters.summary: The town buries the nameless maid under her recovered name beside a new stone for Edith. Tarnow, testifying freely now, lays flowers on both graves. Emotional beat: mourning done properly at last—memory restored its price paid.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: Casper must choose: return to her invisible life in London or stay. She and Brightwater negotiate something honest and unhurried, neither surrendering the work that defines them. Emotional beat: quiet joy—love chosen, not sacrificed to duty.

chapters.title: The Next Impossible Paper
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Casper's POV. Months later, a letter arrives: another will that shouldn't exist, in another coastal town. She packs her bag, and this time she isn't alone. Emotional beat: forward motion—the invisible woman visible, and unafraid.
